title: Prime-module acyclic-resolution comparison criterion
statement: Let $i:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $r$ a prime. Suppose restriction on global sections is an isomorphism for every sheaf of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and the inverse image of every injective such module sheaf has zero positive underlying abelian cohomology [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then for every abelian etale sheaf $G$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] killed by $r$, and every $q\geq0$, the canonical pullback $H^q(X,G)\to H^q(Y,i^{-1}G)$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is bijective.

proof.text: The equation r times id G = 0 makes each section group a canonical Z/r-module. Restrictions are linear, so this is a module sheaf, with underlying abelian sheaf canonically G. ULift changes only the universe of the coefficient ring.

Choose an injective resolution in prime-module sheaves. Forgetting to abelian sheaves is exact and its terms are cohomologically acyclic by 03FD. Inverse image is exact; the assumed restriction acyclicity makes the restricted resolution acyclic on Y as well. Leray computes both abelian cohomologies from section complexes.

The assumed global-sections restriction isomorphisms give a termwise isomorphism of these complexes, hence bijections on homology in all degrees. Compare into abelian injective resolutions on X and Y. Naturality of restriction gives the commuting square; homotopy uniqueness makes the induced comparison independent of lifts. Thus these homology maps are the canonical cohomologyMap, rather than unspecified bijections.
